title: Road Building
strapline: Roads that join up, bridges that hold, a whole town to drive through — the engineering behind every journey.
intent: Building roads, junctions and bridges is real construction and engineering — children plan a network, test whether it connects and rebuild what fails.
Making roads that actually join up, and bridges strong enough to cross, is a genuine problem children solve through trial, adjustment and cooperation.
Laying track, blocks and tiles into a working layout develops fine-motor precision and spatial reasoning.
A road network invites rich positional and directional language — the road bends round here, the bridge goes over there, this way leads to the garage.
Designing a town or route to drive through connects construction to children's real experience of streets, journeys and places.
It is deeply collaborative — children negotiate a shared plan, divide the work and problem-solve together.
implementation: Offer blocks, planks, road tiles, guttering, tape and vehicles, and leave the layout open so children design and redesign it.
Pose real engineering challenges: 'can you build a road that joins the garage to the shop?', 'a bridge the lorry can cross without it falling?'
Step back and let children plan, test and rebuild — the redesigning is where the thinking is.
Narrate position and direction alongside them: 'the road bends round the corner, then over the bridge, past the station'.
Add signs, junctions, a roundabout and mark-making so children plan and label their network.
Take it big outdoors with chalk roads and ride-ons, or small indoors with track and cars — both build the same thinking.
key_questions: Can you build a road that joins the garage to the shop?
How could you make a bridge the lorry can cross without it falling?
The road bends round here — then where does it lead?
What happened when it fell down — what could you change?
Which way should this junction go?
